stem: Alok copies every house number from $70$ to $79$ into his notebook. He wants the number of times the digit $7$ is written in that list.

parts.text: Which claim correctly counts the digit $7$?

options.text: The digit $7$ is written $11$ times, because each tens place contributes one $7$ and $77$ contributes one extra $7$.
The digit $7$ is written $10$ times, counting only how many house numbers are in the list.
The digit $7$ is written once, because the list is about the chosen digit $7$.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: Each written appearance of the digit counts, so the ten tens-place sevens plus the extra units digit in 77 give 11.

teacher.key_rationale: From 70 to 79 the tens digit is 7 ten times, and 77 has a second 7 in the units place, so the digit is written 11 times. Counting numbers in the list or treating the chosen digit as a single mark undercounts appearances.
